mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) over the past 3 months signals an easing monetary policy, which reduces the discount rate for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS declines over the past 3 months, or the Rank IC for the signal is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6.0% within the past month indicates deteriorating labor market conditions, which triggers risk-off sentiment and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 60% of instances where UNRATE > 6.0%, or the Rank IC for the signal is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 107.0 index points and rise in consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above 2.0% signals stagflation, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of instances where INDPRO < 107.0 and CPIAUCSL > 2.0%, or the Rank IC for the signal is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 2.0% and rising), a decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 800.0 thousand units signals a weakening housing market, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 2.0% and rising and HOUST < 800.0, or the Rank IC for the signal is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
